Looking at the folds: the octagon is folded along the vertical axis, then the horizontal axis, then along a diagonal, producing a triangle whose vertical side lies on the first fold line and whose apex is a vertex of the octagon.

The cut is made perpendicular to the vertical (folded) side, at the level of the apex. Unfolding the third fold reflects this cut into a vertical cut; unfolding the second and first folds reflects these cuts across the horizontal and vertical axes.

Result: each of the four "axis" vertices of the octagon (top, bottom, left, right) is sliced off by a straight cut perpendicular to the fold line, while the diagonal vertices remain (as slightly trimmed corners). The unfolded shape is therefore a square-like figure with flat top, bottom, left, right sides and small chamfered corners at the diagonals.

This matches option C.
